Article_Title: Bosch warns production at risk as Nexperia dispute hits auto suppliers
Article_Text:

Seeking alternatives, pooling inventories

German auto parts supplier Bosch is preparing to furlough staff at its Salzgitter plant if a trade dispute between China and the Netherlands over Dutch chipmaker Nexperia is not resolved soon, amid mounting concerns in Europe's beleaguered car industry.Bosch and other suppliers are scrambling for alternatives after China banned exports of Nexperia's finished products in response to the Netherlands seizing control of the company, whose Chinese owner Wingtech has been flagged by the US as a possible national security risk.Because Nexperia's chips are widely used in car parts, the stand-off risks adding to problems for Europe's auto sector on top of US tariffs and Chinese curbs on rare earths."We are currently doing everything we can to serve our customers and avoid or minimise production restrictions," a Bosch spokesperson said in an emailed statement to Reuters."We have not yet made any adjustments to working hours at our German locations, but are preparing to do so, particularly in Salzgitter," she said, adding that potential furlough measures were being prepared at the plant.Salzgitter is Bosch's lead plant for motor control units for combustion and electric vehicles, and employs about 1,400 staff.Earlier on Friday, Volkswagen said it had secured production in Germany for the coming work week across the group, which includes the core VW brand and luxury subsidiary Porsche."In view of the dynamic situation, however, short-term impacts on the production network of the Volkswagen Group cannot generally be ruled out," a spokesperson said.BMW and Mercedes have also warned that their supplier networks are affected.A regional representative of Germany's IG Metall union warned on Friday of a worsening situation.Some automotive suppliers are already seeing "severe difficulties" and have started to announce furlough schemes for workers, Horst Ott, IG Metall district manager in the southern state of Bavaria, said at an industry event in Munich.He did not mention any companies by name.Bosch said it was drawing on alternative suppliers and optimising inventories in its global production network in a bid to prevent production stoppages.Most Nexperia chips are manufactured in Europe but packaged in China.Industry sources say switching suppliers is possible, with Infineon, NXP and Texas Instruments possible alternatives, but this takes time due to approval processes.Auto industry bodies have called for a political solution.Dutch Prime Minister Dick Schoof discussed the situation with other European leaders during an EU summit in Brussels this week.

Article_Title: Nexperia’s Chinese owner warns Dutch government: ‘If control of Nexperia cannot be restored before…’
Article_Text:
Dutch government seize control of Nexperia’s Chinese unit







Nexperia’s Chinese parent company, Wingtech Technology, has issued a formal warning to the Dutch government, stating that its financial performance may take a major hit if it fails to regain control of its seized chipmaking unit, Nexperia, by the end of 2025. In its latest quarterly earnings report filed on Friday (October 24), the Shanghai-listed electronics firm warned of significant financial strain.“If control of Nexperia cannot be restored before the end of 2025, the company may face temporary downward pressure on revenue, profit and cash flow,” Bloomberg stated Wingtech as saying.The warning underscores the escalating international conflict centred on the critical semiconductor supplier. While Wingtech reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings, with semiconductor revenue rising 12.2% year-on-year, the company noted that the long-term ability of its chipmaking segment to sustain growth is now in doubt due to the ongoing dispute.The clash began last month when the Dutch government took the step of seizing control of Nexperia, a key manufacturer of basic chips used widely in the automotive industry by companies like Volkswagen AG.Reports suggested that the seizure followed mounting US pressure after Wingtech was placed on the US Entity List in 2024. The Dutch government cited concerns that Nexperia will not operate independently of its Chinese parent, resulting in the removal of Nexperia's Chinese CEO.According to the report, the dispute is fueling concerns over global supply chain stability ahead of US-China trade talks. Earlier this week, China's commerce minister warned that the Dutch action has “seriously affected” the stability of the global supply chain. The Dutch government, in its replay, has stated it remains in contact with Chinese authorities, aiming to work “toward a constructive solution.”
